-- CH-02: what still needs verifying?
--
-- The work queue is DERIVED FROM THE DATA rather than held in a queue table.
-- An interrupted run therefore resumes correctly, a business is never
-- verified twice, and there is no queue to drift out of sync with reality.
--
-- The cctlds come from the search target, so a Norwegian salon gets .no
-- probed before .com and a Spanish one gets .es. Without this join the domain
-- prover would burn its probe budget on the wrong guesses in every country
-- except the United States.

SELECT
  b.id,
  b.google_place_id,
  b.niche,
  b.name,
  b.name_norm,
  b.city,
  b.country,
  b.phone_e164,
  b.email,
  b.geohash7,
  b.lat,
  b.lon,
  b.rating,
  b.review_count,
  b.address,
  b.social_profiles,
  b.permanently_closed,
  b.raw ->> 'website'            AS source_website_raw,
  -- A search recorded by hand (stage-c-search.js uses it instead of Serper).
  b.raw -> 'hand_search'         AS hand_search,
  COALESCE(t.cctlds, ARRAY['.com'])  AS cctlds,
  COALESCE(t.min_lead_score, 60)     AS min_lead_score,
  t.niche_query
FROM businesses b
LEFT JOIN search_targets t ON t.id = b.search_target_id
WHERE b.website_status = 'PENDING'
  AND b.permanently_closed = false
  -- Verify on demand. Every lead costs a Serper search, and CH-02 used to
  -- verify ~1,400 a day for a sender that sends 30: the 2,500 free credits
  -- on a fresh key were gone in twelve hours (5-6 Oct 2026) while 943
  -- verified leads and 183 approved messages sat unused. Now nothing is
  -- verified while the approved queue holds $2 or more messages.
  AND ((SELECT count(*) FROM outreach WHERE status = 'approved') < $2::int
       -- Searched by hand on purpose: verify now, whatever the queue.
       OR b.raw ? 'hand_search')
ORDER BY
  -- Hand-searched first, and a batch of them never calls Serper at all, so
  -- they get through even while the key is refused.
  (b.raw ? 'hand_search') DESC,
  -- A lead with an email can be written to; one without only reaches the
  -- WhatsApp list, which has hundreds verified already.
  (coalesce(b.email, '') <> '') DESC,
  -- Businesses with more reviews are more likely to be worth the verification
  -- spend, so they go first when the batch limit bites.
  b.review_count DESC NULLS LAST,
  b.first_seen_at ASC
LIMIT $1::int;

parameters.query:
-- CH-02 Stage B: cross-check a candidate against the free open datasets.
--
-- This is the highest-leverage query in the project and it costs nothing to
-- run. Google Maps says this business has no website; Overture and Foursquare
-- are independent of Google and may well hold one. If they do, Stage A was
-- wrong and we have caught a false positive for zero marginal cost.
--
-- Three match strategies, in descending order of confidence. The strongest
-- one that hits wins.
--
--   1. phone in E.164     - two listings sharing a phone number are the same
--                           business, whatever they call themselves
--   2. name + geohash7    - same normalised name inside the same ~150m cell
--   3. name + load_city   - weakest. Used only to establish PRESENCE in the
--                           dataset, never on its own to assert a website,
--                           because two salons with the same name in one city
--                           is entirely plausible.
--
--  Strategy 3 compares against load_city - the city WE searched for - not the
--  dataset's own locality field. Overture stores the locality as the upstream
--  provider wrote it, which for Dubai is Arabic. Comparing Google's "Dubai"
--  against that can never match, so this fallback silently ceased to exist for
--  the whole Gulf until it was noticed in the loaded data.
--
-- match_rank is returned so the caller can tell how much to trust the answer
-- rather than treating all three as equivalent.

WITH candidate AS (
  SELECT
    $1::text AS place_id,
    $2::text AS name_norm,
    $3::text AS phone_e164,
    $4::text AS geohash7,
    $5::text AS city
),

overture AS (
  SELECT
    'overture'::text AS src,
    o.gers_id        AS ref_id,
    o.websites,
    o.socials,
    o.confidence,
    o.operating_status,
    CASE
      WHEN c.phone_e164 <> '' AND o.phone_e164 = c.phone_e164        THEN 1
      WHEN c.geohash7   <> '' AND o.geohash7   = c.geohash7
                              AND o.name_norm  = c.name_norm          THEN 2
      WHEN lower(o.load_city) = lower(c.city) AND o.name_norm = c.name_norm THEN 3
    END AS match_rank
  FROM ref_overture_places o
  CROSS JOIN candidate c
  -- A business CH-00 found IN Overture would otherwise match its own record
  -- and earn "an open dataset holds no website for them" - the dataset
  -- vouching for itself. Its own row is excluded; any OTHER record still counts.
  WHERE ('ovt:' || o.gers_id) <> c.place_id
    AND ((c.phone_e164 <> '' AND o.phone_e164 = c.phone_e164)
     OR (c.geohash7   <> '' AND o.geohash7   = c.geohash7 AND o.name_norm = c.name_norm)
     OR (lower(o.load_city) = lower(c.city) AND o.name_norm = c.name_norm))
),

fsq AS (
  SELECT
    'fsq'::text       AS src,
    f.fsq_place_id    AS ref_id,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(f.website, '') <> '' THEN ARRAY[f.website] ELSE '{}'::text[] END AS websites,
    ARRAY_REMOVE(ARRAY[f.facebook_id, f.instagram, f.twitter], NULL) AS socials,
    NULL::numeric     AS confidence,
    CASE WHEN f.date_closed IS NOT NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE NULL END AS operating_status,
    CASE
      WHEN c.phone_e164 <> '' AND f.tel_e164 = c.phone_e164          THEN 1
      WHEN c.geohash7   <> '' AND f.geohash7 = c.geohash7
                              AND f.name_norm = c.name_norm           THEN 2
      WHEN lower(f.load_city) = lower(c.city) AND f.name_norm = c.name_norm THEN 3
    END AS match_rank
  FROM ref_fsq_places f
  CROSS JOIN candidate c
  WHERE (c.phone_e164 <> '' AND f.tel_e164 = c.phone_e164)
     OR (c.geohash7   <> '' AND f.geohash7 = c.geohash7 AND f.name_norm = c.name_norm)
     OR (lower(f.load_city) = lower(c.city) AND f.name_norm = c.name_norm)
),

matches AS (
  SELECT * FROM overture
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM fsq
)

SELECT
  (SELECT place_id FROM candidate)                       AS place_id,
  COUNT(*) > 0                                           AS matched,
  MIN(match_rank)                                        AS best_match_rank,
  -- A website only counts when the match that produced it was rank 1 or 2.
  -- A name-and-city match is not strong enough to attach somebody else's
  -- website to this business, and doing so would turn a real prospect into a
  -- discarded HAS_WEBSITE.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT w
     FROM matches m, unnest(m.websites) AS w
     WHERE m.match_rank <= 2 AND COALESCE(w, '') <> ''
     LIMIT 1),
    ''
  )                                                      AS website,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT s)
     FROM matches m, unnest(m.socials) AS s
     WHERE COALESCE(s, '') <> ''),
    '{}'::text[]
  )                                                      AS socials,
  BOOL_OR(operating_status = 'closed')                   AS looks_closed,
  MIN(confidence)                                        AS min_confidence,
  COALESCE(array_agg(DISTINCT src), '{}'::text[])        AS sources
FROM matches;

parameters.query:
-- CH-02: record the verdict and the evidence that produced it.
--
-- Two writes in one statement, deliberately atomic:
--
--   1. website_checks gets every check that ran, append-only. This is what
--      makes a classification auditable and, more usefully, RE-DERIVABLE: if
--      the confidence thresholds change, old rows can be re-scored offline
--      without re-scraping or re-paying for anything.
--
--   2. businesses gets the verdict itself.
--
-- The WHERE clause on the UPDATE is a guard, not decoration. A verdict is
-- only written over PENDING. If two CH-02 executions overlap - which a
-- 30-minute schedule and a slow probe batch make entirely possible - the
-- second one finds the row already decided and leaves it alone rather than
-- overwriting a verdict with a staler one.

WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO website_checks (business_id, stage, method, candidate_url, outcome, evidence)
  SELECT
    $1::bigint,
    c ->> 'stage',
    c ->> 'method',
    NULLIF(c ->> 'candidate_url', ''),
    c ->> 'outcome',
    COALESCE(c -> 'evidence', '{}'::jsonb)
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) AS c
  RETURNING 1
)
UPDATE businesses SET
  website_status     = $3,
  website_confidence = $4,
  website_url        = NULLIF($5, ''),
  website_evidence   = $6,
  website_checked_at = now(),
  -- $7 is Stage F's finding, if it ran. COALESCE onto the existing value so a
  -- re-verify never erases an email a human or an earlier run already found.
  email               = COALESCE(NULLIF($7, ''), businesses.email)
WHERE id = $1::bigint
  AND website_status = 'PENDING'
RETURNING id, website_status, website_confidence;
-- The count of inserted checks is deliberately NOT returned. Referencing a
-- data-modifying CTE from the outer RETURNING is subtle enough to be worth
-- avoiding for a number nothing reads; the CTE still runs either way, because
-- Postgres always executes a data-modifying CTE whether or not it is
-- referenced.

nodes.notes: This runs 48 times a day. Reporting 'nothing to verify' every half hour trains you to scroll past the message, and then you scroll past the one that matters.

parameters.content:
## CH-02 — Verify the website gap

**This is the workflow the project stands or falls on.**

CH-01 produces candidates. A candidate is a business whose Google Maps listing carries no website field. That is *not* the same as a business without a website, and the entire value of the lead list depends on the difference.

### The five stages, cheapest first

| | Stage | Costs | Catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | What did the listing claim? | free | social-only, Linktree, dead `business.site` |
| B | Cross-check Overture + Foursquare | **free, unlimited** | the owner has a site, just never added it to Maps |
| C | Search for them | ~$0.001 | a site under a name we would never guess |
| D | Guess a domain and **prove** it | free | the rest |
| E | PageSpeed | free | a site that exists but is unusable |
| F | Find a contact email | free | only possible for HAS_WEBSITE / WEAK_WEBSITE - a confirmed no-website lead has nowhere for this to look, which is why outreach for those defaults to phone |

Each stage that *completes* adds confidence. Each stage that cannot run leaves it lower. That is the whole mechanism:

> **"We checked and found nothing" and "we could not check" must never produce the same number.**

### Why there are no IF branches here

Every stage skips itself when an earlier one already settled the question. The flow stays linear, so there are no Merge nodes and no item-pairing bugs — the failure mode where one business's answer gets attached to another business.

Stage B re-pairs **by place id, not by position**, for the same reason.

### Setup

1. Load the reference data first — Stage B is worthless against empty tables:
   ```
   python tools/load_overture.py --city Oslo --country Norway
   python tools/load_fsq.py --city Oslo --country Norway
   ```
2. Optional: a Serper key in `Config` enables Stage C. Without it the pipeline still works, but confidence caps lower and fewer leads reach CONFIRMED. That is correct behaviour, not a bug.
3. Optional: a PageSpeed key raises the rate limit. The API works without one.

### Read this number in the report

**"False positives caught"** — businesses whose listing said no website and which turned out to have one. Every one of those is an email that would have opened *"I noticed you don't have a website"* to somebody who does. If that number is zero on a batch of 20+, check the reference tables are actually populated for that city.
